content: This medication, Tobramycin, is used to treat bacterial eye infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as aminoglycoside antibiotics and is effective only against bacterial infections, not other types of eye infections. To use the eye drops, first wash your hands thoroughly. Avoid wearing contact lenses while using this medication. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above your eye and place one drop into the pouch. Look downward and gently close your eyes for 1 to 2 minutes. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eye. Do not rinse the dropper after use. If you are using other eye medications, wait at least 5 to 10 minutes before applying them. Use this medication regularly at the same times each day to achieve the best results. Continue using it for the full duration prescribed, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include tearing, eye redness, discomfort, or itching/swelling of the eyelid. These effects are usually mild. However, prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to a new fungal eye infection. Do not use it for longer than prescribed. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. If you experience severe symptoms such as difficulty breathing or swelling, seek immediate medical attention. Before using Tobramycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other aminoglycosides (e.g., gentamicin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as preservatives like benzalkonium chloride, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. After applying the medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred or unstable. Use caution when performing activities that require clear vision. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as its effects on breast milk are unknown. Inform your doctor of all medications and products you are using to avoid potential drug interactions, which may alter the effectiveness of your treatment or increase the risk of side effects. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication according to the instructions provided on the product packaging, as storage requirements may vary by brand. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. In case of overdose, this medication may be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Do not use it for other conditions or share it with others. Discard any unused medication after completing your treatment. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
